citations: Fortera has signed a multi-year agreement with Meta covering environmental attribute certificates (EACs) associated with approximately 200,000 tons of its low-carbon cement, in a deal designed to help finance production expansion.
Meta will also have the option to use the cement in its own construction projects and expand the agreement’s volume or duration in future years.
The partnership is expected to support development of Fortera’s planned cement plant in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri.

The facility is designed to produce ReAct Cement, which uses captured carbon dioxide (CO2) and, according to Fortera, generates 70% fewer emissions than ordinary Portland cement production. The product has undergone third-party testing and meets ASTM standards for use in concrete.
The plant is planned to produce 300,000 tons of cement annually. Fortera already operates a facility in Redding, California, with annual capacity of 15,000 tons.

citations: Montreal, November 2, 2026 – CarbiCrete, a leading firm in the decarbonization of concrete, has supplied Amazon with three different products at a new Amazon UK delivery station in Stockton-on-Tees.
In the first wide-scale deployment of its cement-free pavers anywhere in the world, CarbiCrete products now cover around 6,400m² of paving across parking spaces and footpaths at the site.

The delivery station is Amazon’s first building to pursue the latest version (v1.1) of Living Future’s Zero Carbon Certification, a rigorous standard that sets demanding requirements for both construction and operations.

CarbiCrete’s technology replaces 100% of the cement content in masonry and hardscape products with a steel-making by-product, avoiding cement-related emissions. The company then uses carbon dioxide to cure its concrete, permanently storing captured carbon within the products, significantly lowering the embodied carbon of the construction projects in which they are used.
“Seeing CarbiCrete products deployed at this scale is an important milestone for our technology and for lower-carbon construction more broadly.,” says Gary Belisle, CarbiCrete’s CEO.
